newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CLASSIC IN PROSPECT AS UNITED FACE DORTMUND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CLASSIC IN PROSPECT AS UNITED FACE DORTMUND.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund visit Manchester United for the second leg of their European Cup semifinal on Wednesday knowing their 1-0 first leg advantage will probably not be enough to win them the match.
Coach Ottmar Hitzfeld said before leaving Germany on Tuesday: "One goal won't be enough. We will need to come out and attack and I think we will need one or two more goals to get to the final."

A major battle is in prospect at the Theatre of Dreams, where no German side has ever beaten United. Hitzfeld says his team will go for goals, and as that is precisely what United intend, the match could be a classic.
Borussia won the first leg two weeks ago thanks to a late goal from Rene Tretschok who may find himself on the bench this time.

That is partly because Hitzfeld is able to welcome back several players from injury or suspension -- although he may again be without European Player of the Year Matthias Sammer, who was suspended from the first leg and is almost certainly out with a torn thigh muscle.
But Hitzfeld hopes to welcome back Portugese midfielder Paulo Sousa and wing back Stefan Reuter, who both missed Saturday's 1-1 draw with Bayern Munich due to torn muscles.
Ghanian striker Ibrahim Tanko may also be available for selection after injury but is unlikely to play from the start as Stephane Chapuisat and Karlheinz Riedle are both fit.
But it is Sammer's injury which could prove decisive. Sammer has been plagued by problems this season, playing in only 13 of Dortmund's 28 league games and four of their nine European Cup ties.
The persistent injuries, and the fact Sammer was not in Dortmund's Westfalen Stadium for the Bayern game, have sparked reports he may even be thinking of ending his career.
"I'm so sick of these injuries, "he said, "I am seriously considering packing up and retiring early.
"I need to get some expert advice to see if I can carry on, but I can't go on suffering one injury after another and not being able to play."
Juergen Kohler, who missed the first leg through injury, knows the German champions will face an onslaught from United as they attempt to overturn the 1-0 deficit.
"We won't have many chances so we have to be ice cool and exploit the ones we do get," Kohler said.
On their day United are one of the best counter-attacking teams in Europe, turning defence into attack in two or three devastating moves.
The club are currently on a high having virtually ensured their fourth English championship in five years after beating Liverpool 3-1 on Saturday.

United will be without battling midfielder Roy Keane who is suspended. United manager Alex Ferguson could well move Norwegian defender Ronny Johnsen into the midfield role vacated by Keane especially if central defender David May returns from injury.

The prize at stake is the European Cup final in Munich on May 28. If Borussia win they will be in their first European Cup final, should United win they will reach their first final in the competition since 1968 when they beat Benfica.
United will have to be at their absolute peak to succeed -- and inspired by a 50,000-plus home crowd, they might reach that summit.

Manchester United (from): Peter Schmeichel; Gary Neville, Philip Neville, Ronnie Johnsen, David May, Gary Pallister, Eric Cantona, Nicky Butt, David Beckham, Andy Cole, Paul Scholes, Ole Solskjaer, Ryan Giggs, Brian McClair.
Borussia Dortmund: Stefan Klos; Wolfgang Feiersinger, Stefan Reuter, Juergen Kohler, Martin Kree, Joerg Heinrich, Paul Lambert, Paulo Sousa, Andy Moeller; Stephane Chapuisat, Karlheinz Riedle.
